title: Linear Inequalities and Their Graphs
seo_title: Linear Inequalities – SSS 2 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Solve linear inequalities in one variable; solve simultaneous inequalities; show solutions on a number line and on a graph; solve word problems. (summary of the NERDC SSS 2 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 2 maths worksheets on inequalities: solving linear inequalities, combined inequalities, number lines, graphs of regions and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiplying by a negative turns the sign round
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Solve an inequality like an equation.
  • When you multiply or divide by a negative number, reverse the sign.
  • On a graph, test a point such as (0, 0) to find which side of the line is the region.

Examples

Example

3 − 2x ≤ 9

−2x ≤ 6

Answer: x ≥ −3

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not turning the signTurn it when dividing by a negative.
Shading the wrong sideTest a point.
Using a solid line for << and > use a broken line.

items.q: Solve −x − 5 < −5x + 3. Write the solution as an interval.
items.e: Collect x on one side: 4x < 8, so x < 2. The solution set is (−∞, 2).

items.q:
Is (−3, 4) a solution of the system?
y ≥ −2x − 2
y ≥ 23x
c: No, it only works in the first
No, it only works in the second
items.e: First: 4 ≥ 4 is true. Second: 4 ≥ −2 is true. It works in both, so yes.

items.q:
Is (−4, −2) a solution of the system?
y ≥ −x − 2
y < 3x + 1
c: No, it only works in the second
No, it only works in the first
items.e: First: −2 ≥ 2 is false. Second: −2 < −11 is false. A solution must work in both, so no.

c: No, it only works in the first
No, it only works in the second

items.q: Which system is shown? The solution region is where the two shadings overlap.
items.e: Blue line y = −1: solid, shaded below. Red line y = −3x − 3: solid, shaded above. So y ≤ −1 and y ≥ −3x − 3.

items.q: Which system is shown? The solution region is where the two shadings overlap.
items.e: Blue line y = 3x − 2: solid, shaded below. Red line y = 12x + 1: solid, shaded above. So y ≤ 3x − 2 and y ≥ 12x + 1.

items.q: Which system is shown? The solution region is where the two shadings overlap.
items.e: Blue line y = −3x + 2: solid, shaded above. Red line y = 3x − 2: solid, shaded above. So y ≥ −3x + 2 and y ≥ 3x − 2.

items.q: Which system is shown? The solution region is where the two shadings overlap.
items.e: Blue line y = x − 1: solid, shaded above. Red line y = −3: dashed, shaded below. So y ≥ x − 1 and y < −3.

items.q: Which system is shown? The solution region is where the two shadings overlap.

items.q: Which system is shown? The solution region is where the two shadings overlap.

items.q: Which system is shown? The solution region is where the two shadings overlap.

items.e: Blue line y = −2x − 2: solid, shaded above. Red line y = −3x − 2: solid, shaded below. So y ≥ −2x − 2 and y ≤ −3x − 2.

items.q: x satisfies both 4x − 4 > −24 and −2x − 3 ≥ −5. List the integer values of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x > −5 and x ≤ 1, so −5 < x ≤ 1. The integers are −4, −3, −2, −1, 0, 1.

items.q: x satisfies both −2x − 5 < −11 and −2x − 3 > −19. List the integer values of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x > 3 and x < 8, so 3 < x < 8. The integers are 4, 5, 6, 7.

items.q: x satisfies both −3x + 5 ≤ 8 and 5x − 6 ≤ 19. Find the greatest integer value of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x ≥ −1 and x ≤ 5, so −1 ≤ x ≤ 5. The greatest integer is 5.

items.q: x satisfies both −3x − 2 < 4 and 3x ≤ 0. Find the greatest integer value of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x > −2 and x ≤ 0, so −2 < x ≤ 0. The greatest integer is 0.

items.q: x satisfies both 4x − 5 > −9 and 5x − 1 < 9. Find the smallest integer value of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x > −1 and x < 2, so −1 < x < 2. The smallest integer is 0 (−1 itself is not allowed).

items.q: x satisfies both 2x + 5 > −7 and −2x > 6. Find the range of values of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x > −6 and x < −3, so −6 < x < −3. −6 < x < −3.

items.q: x satisfies both −2x − 1 ≤ −1 and 3x + 5 ≤ 23. Find the range of values of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x ≥ 0 and x ≤ 6, so 0 ≤ x ≤ 6. 0 ≤ x ≤ 6.

items.q: x satisfies both −3x + 1 < 13 and 5x + 5 < 10. List the integer values of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x > −4 and x < 1, so −4 < x < 1. The integers are −3, −2, −1, 0.

items.q: x satisfies both 3x + 1 ≥ 10 and 5x + 1 ≤ 36. List the integer values of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x ≥ 3 and x ≤ 7, so 3 ≤ x ≤ 7. The integers are 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.

items.q: x satisfies both −3x + 3 ≤ 21 and x − 2 ≤ −4. List the integer values of x.
items.e: Solve each one: x ≥ −6 and x ≤ −2, so −6 ≤ x ≤ −2. The integers are −6, −5, −4, −3, −2.

items.q: How many integers x satisfy -3 < 6x − 3 < 9?
items.e: Dividing through: 0 < x < 2, so x = 1, …, 1: 1 integers.

items.q: Solve 5x + 9 ≤ 24 when x is a natural number.
items.e: x ≤ 3. The natural numbers that fit are {1, 2, 3}.

items.q: How many integers x satisfy -29 < 6x − 5 < 25?
items.e: Dividing through: -4 < x < 5, so x = -3, …, 4: 8 integers.
